newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller warns of Islamist-secularist split.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller warns of Islamist-secularist split.

text.p: Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller on Wednesday warned against a polarisation of society between secularists and Islamists amid a row over a military-led bid to curb religious activism.

"Do not set people against one another by declaring them as secular or religious," Ciller told members of her True Path Party (DYP), the junior partner in coalition with Islamists. "The most blood that has been shed since the Cold War came to an end...was by groups within countries which hate each other."
Turkey's powerful National Security Council (NSC) has called on the coalition to crack down on a rise in Islam-based activism since it came to power last June.
The call has raised tensions between Islamists and the secular establishment and strained the government alliance.

One of the military demands -- to raise compulsory state education to eight years from five -- has provoked opposition from Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party, which sees the measure as a threat to the role of religious schools.
Ciller, who is also the foreign minister, said on Wednesday the eight-year schooling plan would be pushed through. She cautioned against describing the security council demands as "irreligious".
"If we set the army against religion, the greatest damage will be inflicted on this country," she said.
